lessons.title: Phrasen
lessons.notes_html:
The W-question words

Wie?How?কেমন/কীভাবে?
Was?What?কী?
Wo?Where?কোথায়?
Woher?From where?কোথা থেকে?
Wann?When?কখন?
Warum?Why?কেন?
Wie viel?How much?কত?

Trap: Wo = where (not who!), Was = what.

“I have hunger”, not “I am hungry”

German uses haben (have) for hunger, thirst and time:

Ich habe Hunger. · Ich habe Durst. · Ich habe Zeit.

But sein (be) for tired, ready, finished, age:

Ich bin müde. · Ich bin fertig. · Ich bin 30 Jahre alt.

বাংলার মতো: "আমার খিদে আছে" = Ich habe Hunger।

kein vs. nicht

kein / keine = “no / not any” before a thing (noun): kein Problem · keine Zeit · keine Ahnung

nicht = “not” with an action or description: Ich verstehe nicht. · Ich weiß nicht.

kein = কোনো … নেই, nicht = না

lessons.title: Einfache Sätze
lessons.notes_html:
The verb sits in seat 2

In a normal sentence the verb is always the 2nd element:

Ich koche heute.
Heute koche ich.

বাংলায় ক্রিয়া শেষে থাকে (আমি আজ রান্না করছি), জার্মানে দ্বিতীয় স্থানে।

Nouns start with a capital

Every German noun is capitalized: Buch, Wasser, Zeit, Hund, Film, Hilfe. Easy way to spot the nouns in a sentence!

Each noun also has a gender: der Hund, die Zeit, das Buch. Learn the article with the word.
